stem:
Vihaan studies three pairs near a farm pond: rhizobium bacteria in pea-plant roots that help the plant get nitrogen while the bacteria get food; a fern growing on a mango trunk without harming the tree; and lice living on a buffalo and harming it.

How should he classify the three relationships?

options.text: Pea plant and rhizobium: mutualism. Fern and mango: commensalism. Lice and buffalo: parasitism.
Pea plant and rhizobium: parasitism. Fern and mango: mutualism. Lice and buffalo: commensalism.
All three are mutualism because each pair lives close together.
Fern and mango: parasitism, because the fern sits on the mango.

teacher.key_rationale: Mutualism: both benefit; commensalism: one benefits, other unaffected; parasitism: one benefits, other harmed.
